docs.title: About
docs.text: TSFX is a Python library for extracting features from time series data. Inspired by the great TSFresh library, TSFX aims to provide a similar feature set focused on performance on large datasets. In order to achieve this, TSFX is built on top of the Polars DataFrame library, and feature extractors are implemented in Rust.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Extracting the 201 features TSFX, functime and TSFresh all implement (efficient tier, TSFresh's default parameters) from the 1 Billion Row Challenge data (8,859 series), on a 2× Xeon Gold 6230 (80 threads, 503 GB RAM). Best of three runs, one run at 1B:

rows TSFX functime TSFresh vs functime vs TSFresh 1M 0.137 s 3.62 s 15.2 s 26x 111x 10M 0.72 s 31.1 s 20.1 s 43x 28x 100M 6.9 s 313 s 70 s 45x 10x 1B 84.8 s –¹ 643 s – 8x

¹ functime ran out of memory (it peaked at 257 GB at 100M rows).

To reproduce, see python_benchmarks/library_compare.py and python_benchmarks/1brc.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
For most common platforms and architectures, pre-built wheels are available. You can install the package directly from PyPI:

pip install tsfx

docs.title: Installing from Source (Unsupported Targets)
docs.text:
If a pre-built wheel is not available for your specific platform, pip will automatically attempt to build the package from the source distribution (sdist).

Because tsfx is built with Maturin and its core features are implemented in Rust, you will need a Rust compiler to build it from source. Important: Building from source requires a nightly Rust toolchain. The exact nightly is pinned in rust-toolchain.toml to match the Polars version TSFX is built against.

To set up your environment for a source build:

  1. Install Rust (if you haven't already) using rustup: bash curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh

  2. Nightly toolchain: with rustup, the pinned nightly from rust-toolchain.toml is installed and used automatically when building in the source directory. No rustup default nightly is needed.

  3. Install the package: bash pip install tsfx pip will now use your nightly Rust compiler to build the package for your target.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Below is a simple example of extracting features from a time series dataset:

import polars as pl
from tsfx import (
    ExtractionSettings,
    FeatureSetting,
    extract_features,
)

df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": ["a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b", "c", "c", "c"],
        "val": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0],
        "value": [4.0, 5.0, 6.0, 6.0, 5.0, 4.0, 4.0, 5.0, 6.0],
    },
).lazy()
settings = ExtractionSettings(
    grouping_cols=["id"],
    feature_setting=FeatureSetting.Efficient,
    value_cols=["val", "value"],
)
gdf = extract_features(df, settings)
gdf = gdf.sort(by="id")
with pl.Config(set_tbl_width_chars=80):
    print(gdf)

docs.title: Extracting over a time window
docs.text:
An additional feature of TSFX is the ability to extract features over a time window. Below is an example of extracting features over a 3 year window:

import polars as pl
from tsfx import (
    DynamicGroupBySettings,
    ExtractionSettings,
    FeatureSetting,
    extract_features,
)

tdf = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": ["a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b", "c", "c", "c"],
        "time": [
            "2001-01-01",
            "2002-01-01",
            "2003-01-01",
            "2001-01-01",
            "2002-01-01",
            "2003-01-01",
            "2001-01-01",
            "2002-01-01",
            "2003-01-01",
        ],
        "val": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0],
        "value": [4.0, 5.0, 6.0, 6.0, 5.0, 4.0, 4.0, 5.0, 6.0],
    },
).lazy()

dyn_settings = DynamicGroupBySettings(
    time_col="time",
    every="3y",
    period="3y",
    offset="0y",
    datetime_format="%Y-%m-%d",
)
settings = ExtractionSettings(
    grouping_cols=["id"],
    value_cols=["val", "value"],
    feature_setting=FeatureSetting.Efficient,
    dynamic_settings=dyn_settings,
)
gdf = extract_features(tdf, settings)
gdf = gdf.sort(by="id")
print(gdf)

which produces the following output:

docs.title: Scaling the features
docs.text:
Features are often scaled before they are used, e.g. to train a model. Pass scaling to scale each feature across the groups (or windows) after extraction: ScalerSetting.Standard() for zero mean and unit variance, or ScalerSetting.MinMax(feature_range=(0, 1)) to map each feature's range onto feature_range. They match scikit-learn's StandardScaler and MinMaxScaler fitted on the feature matrix. NaN, null and infinite values are left out of the fit and kept as they are, and constant features map to 0 (Standard) or the lower end of the range (MinMax). The grouping and time columns are not scaled. The default, scaling=None, leaves the features as extracted.

import polars as pl
from tsfx import ExtractionSettings, FeatureSetting, ScalerSetting, extract_features

df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": ["a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b", "c", "c", "c"],
        "val": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 2.0, 4.0, 6.0, 5.0, 5.0, 5.0],
    },
).lazy()
settings = ExtractionSettings(
    grouping_cols=["id"],
    value_cols=["val"],
    feature_setting=FeatureSetting.Minimal,
    scaling=ScalerSetting.MinMax(feature_range=(-1, 1)),
)
gdf = extract_features(df, settings).sort(by="id")
print(gdf.select("id", "length", "val__mean", "val__maximum", "val__variance"))

which produces the following output:

shape: (3, 5)
┌─────┬────────┬───────────┬──────────────┬───────────────┐
│ id  ┆ length ┆ val__mean ┆ val__maximum ┆ val__variance │
│ --- ┆ ---    ┆ ---       ┆ ---          ┆ ---           │

│ c   ┆ -1.0   ┆ 1.0       ┆ 0.333333     ┆ -1.0          │
└─────┴────────┴───────────┴──────────────┴───────────────┘

docs.title: Reducing redundant features
docs.text:
Many extracted features say the same thing, or nothing. For similarity search in particular, every such feature is an extra dimension: near-copies make one property of the series count many times in a distance, and noise blurs the difference between near and far neighbors. Pass reduction to drop, after extraction and before scaling:

  1. features that are mostly missing: more than max_missing (0.05) of the values null, NaN or infinite;
  2. features that are almost always one value: one value covers more than max_top_share (0.95) of its non-missing values;
  3. near-duplicates: features whose Spearman correlation with an earlier, kept feature is above max_correlation (0.95) in absolute value, e.g. the variance and the standard deviation, or features of two value columns that move together;
  4. noise: features that respect which rows are neighbors no better than shuffled copies of the data (noise_sensitivity, 0.99: about 99% of pure-noise features are dropped).

Each step is turned off with None, e.g. ReductionSetting(noise_sensitivity=None). The columns kept are unchanged, only fewer. The reduction is fitted across the extracted groups (or windows), so it needs several of them (at least 11 with the defaults) and cannot be fitted on a single series. With fewer than 50 features left for the noise step, a UserWarning says it may drop real features as noise, and so does a second one with fewer than 50 rows (groups or windows): the noise step needs enough rows to tell neighbors apart (in tests, it dropped 45% of medium-strength real features at 20 rows, 6% at 40, 2% at 60). The step is strict, keeping a feature only if it beats all 99 shuffled copies, so features with a weak signal and rare flags (a value on a few percent of the rows) are often dropped too; a lower noise_sensitivity (down to 0.5) keeps more of them. The correlation and noise steps work on at most max_samples (5000) rows, a sample drawn with seed, so the result is the same in every run. reduction_report shows what was kept, what was dropped and why (dropped_by is null for a kept feature).

import math

import polars as pl
from tsfx import (
    ExtractionSettings,
    FeatureSetting,
    ReductionSetting,
    extract_features,
    reduction_report,
)

df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": [f"s{g:02}" for g in range(60) for _ in range(200)],
        "val": [
            math.sin(0.1 * (g % 8 + 1) * t) * (1 + g % 5) + 0.02 * g * t
            for g in range(60)
            for t in range(200)
        ],
    },
).lazy()
settings = ExtractionSettings(
    grouping_cols=["id"],
    value_cols=["val"],
    feature_setting=FeatureSetting.Efficient,
    reduction=ReductionSetting(),
)
gdf = extract_features(df, settings)
report = reduction_report(df, settings)
print(f"{report.height} features extracted, {gdf.width - 1} kept")
print(report.group_by("dropped_by").len().sort("len", descending=True))
print(
    report.filter(pl.col("dropped_by") == "duplicate")
    .select("feature", "duplicate_of", "correlation")
    .head(3),
)

which produces the following output:

749 features extracted, 150 kept
shape: (5, 2)
┌────────────┬─────┐
│ dropped_by ┆ len │
│ ---        ┆ --- │
│ str        ┆ u32 │
╞════════════╪═════╡
│ duplicate  ┆ 520 │
│ null       ┆ 150 │
│ one_value  ┆ 61  │
│ noise      ┆ 17  │
│ missing    ┆ 1   │
└────────────┴─────┘
shape: (3, 3)

│ feature      ┆ duplicate_of    ┆ correlation │

docs.title: ExtractionSettings(grouping_cols, value_cols, feature_setting, config_path=None, dynamic_settings=None, scaling=None, reduction=None)
docs.text:
Configuration for a feature extraction run.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default grouping_cols Sequence[str]

Column names used to group rows into separate time series (e.g. an id).

required value_cols Sequence[str]

Column names containing the numeric values to extract features from.

required feature_setting FeatureSetting

One of the FeatureSetting presets controlling which feature calculators run.

required config_path str | None

Optional path to a TOML feature config file; a path that does not exist raises ValueError on extraction. Without one, .tsfx-config.toml in the working directory is used if present, else the default config.

None dynamic_settings DynamicGroupBySettings | None

Optional DynamicGroupBySettings for time-windowed extraction.

None scaling ScalerSetting | type[ScalerSetting] | None

Optional ScalerSetting to scale each feature across groups after extraction, e.g. ScalerSetting.Standard() or ScalerSetting.MinMax(feature_range=(-1, 1)); a variant without arguments may be given without calling it (ScalerSetting.Standard). Defaults to None: no scaling. An invalid feature_range (not finite, or minimum not below maximum) raises ValueError.

None reduction ReductionSetting | None

Optional ReductionSetting to drop redundant and uninformative features after extraction, before scaling. Defaults to None: no reduction.

None

docs.title: FeatureSetting
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

Preset groups of feature extractors.

  • Minimal: smallest, fastest set of features.
  • Efficient: balanced set of commonly useful features (default choice).
  • Comprehensive: largest set of features for maximum coverage.

docs.title: ReductionSetting(max_missing=0.05, max_top_share=0.95, max_correlation=0.95, noise_sensitivity=0.99, noise_neighbors=10, max_samples=5000, seed=0)
docs.text:
How to drop redundant and uninformative features after extraction.

Runs after extraction and before scaling. Drops features that are mostly missing, almost always one value, near-duplicates of an earlier feature (Spearman correlation), or noise (no better than shuffled shadow features at respecting which rows are neighbors). Each step is turned off with None. The reduction is fitted across the extracted rows (groups or windows), so it needs several of them and cannot be fitted on a single series. reduction_report explains every decision.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default max_missing float | None

Drop a feature whose share of missing values (null, NaN, ±inf) is above this, in [0, 1). 0.0 drops every feature with a missing value.

0.05 max_top_share float | None

Drop a feature whose most frequent value covers more than this share of its non-missing values, in (0, 1).

0.95 max_correlation float | None

Drop a feature whose |Spearman correlation| with an earlier kept feature is above this, in (0, 1).

0.95 noise_sensitivity float | None

About this share of pure-noise features is dropped (0.99 lets about 1 in 100 through), in [0.5, 0.999]. Higher is stricter and slower and, with few features left, drops more real features by mistake: with fewer than 50 features or rows reaching the noise step, a UserWarning says so. None turns the step off.

0.99 noise_neighbors int

Nearest rows per row in the noise step, at least 1.

10 max_samples int

Row cap for the correlation and noise steps (a seeded sample above it), larger than noise_neighbors.

5000 seed int

Seed of the row sample and the noise step.

0

docs.title: ScalerSetting
docs.text:
How to scale the extracted features, column-wise across groups.

Matches scikit-learn's StandardScaler and MinMaxScaler fitted on the feature matrix: NaN and null are ignored when fitting and kept in the output, as are infinities (which scikit-learn rejects), and (near-)constant features map to 0 (Standard) or the lower end of the range (MinMax). Grouping and time columns are not scaled, and the scaled features are Float64.

  • Standard(): zero mean and unit (population) variance.
  • MinMax(feature_range=(0, 1)): maps each feature's [min, max] onto feature_range.

docs.title: extract_features(lf, settings, streaming=False)
docs.text:
Extract features from a Polars LazyFrame.

Short wrapper around tsfx.extract_features that runs feature extraction on a Polars LazyFrame and returns a flattened pl.DataFrame. Any Struct columns produced are unnested to top-level columns.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default lf LazyFrame

Input lazy frame.

required settings ExtractionSettings

Extraction configuration.

required streaming bool

Enable streaming mode.

False

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

Flattened DataFrame with extracted features.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the settings are invalid, or settings.reduction cannot be fitted (fewer groups or windows than it needs).

Warns:

Type Description UserWarning

If the reduction's noise step runs on fewer than 50 features or rows: it may then drop real features as noise.

Example 
import polars as pl
from tsfx import ExtractionSettings, FeatureSetting, extract_features

df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": ["a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b", "c", "c", "c"],
        "val": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0],
        "value": [4.0, 5.0, 6.0, 6.0, 5.0, 4.0, 4.0, 5.0, 6.0],
    },
).lazy()

settings = ExtractionSettings(
    grouping_cols=["id"],
    feature_setting=FeatureSetting.Efficient,
    value_cols=["val", "value"],
)

gdf = extract_features(df, settings)

docs.title: reduction_report(lf, settings)
docs.text:
Explain which features the reduction keeps and why.

Extracts the features of lf as settings say (without scaling, which the reduction does not depend on), fits settings.reduction and returns its report: one row per extracted feature, in extraction order, with the columns

  • feature: the feature's column name;
  • kept: whether the reduction keeps it;
  • dropped_by: the step that dropped it ("missing", "one_value", "duplicate" or "noise"), null if kept;
  • missing_share: its share of missing values (null, NaN, ±inf);
  • top_share: the share of its most frequent value among its non-missing values;
  • duplicate_of and correlation: the kept feature it copies, and their Spearman correlation;
  • noise_score and noise_cutoff: its Laplacian score and the best shadow feature's score; it is noise unless its score is below.

A step that is turned off, or that a feature did not reach, leaves its columns null.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default lf LazyFrame

Input lazy frame.

required settings ExtractionSettings

Extraction configuration with a reduction.

required

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

The report.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If settings has no reduction, or the reduction cannot be fitted (e.g. too few groups or windows).

Warns:

Type Description UserWarning

If the noise step runs on fewer than 50 features or rows: it may then drop real features as noise.
